FOREWORD 

This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on 3 November 1989, after 
the draft finalized by Earth Working and Metal Working Tools Sectional Committee had been 
approved by Production Engineering Division Council. 

These types of belt punches are employed for special application for making holes in the conveyor 
belts conforming IS 1891 ( in various parts ) 'Rubber conveyor and elevator belting' in order to 
accommodate the plate type belt fasteners conforming IS 10288 : 1982 'Conveyor belt fasteners, 
plate type'. 

While preparing this specification, considerable assistance has been taken from the details supplied 
by the users and manufacturer of this product. 



IS 12858 : 1989 



Indian Standard 

BELT PUNCHES FOR CONVEYOR BELT 
FASTENERS ( PLATE TYPE ) — SPECIFICATION 



1 SCOPE 

1.1 This Indian Standard covers the dimensions 
and other requirements of belt punches used for 
making holes in conveyor belts for accommodat- 
ing conveyor belt fastener's ( plate type ). 



2 REFERENCES 

IS No. 



Title 



IS 1891 ( in various Rubber conveyor and de- 
parts ) vator belting 

IS 2500 Sampling inspection tables : 

( Part 1 ) : 1973 Part 1 Inspection by attri- 
butes and by count of 
defects 

IS 3749 : 1978 Tool and die steels for cold 

working ( first revision ) 

3 DIMENSIONS 

3.1 Dimension of belt punches shall be as given 
in Table 1. 

4 MATERIAL 

4.1 Belt punches shall be manufactured from 
suitable steels meeting the requirements laid 
down in 5 and 6.2. 

Suitable Example: 

Steel designation 80T3 of IS 3749 : 1978 

5 HARDNESS 

5.1 Belt punches shall be heat-treated up to a 
distance of 25 mm from the cutting edge, to 
achieve hardness between 390 to 510 //P^ ( ^ 40 
to 50 HRC ). 



6 WORKMANSHIP AND FINISH 

6.1 The punches shall be free from burrs, scales, 
seams or any other deleterious defects. The 
shank of the punch shall be knurled as shown in 
the figure under Table 1. 

6.2 Cutting Edge of Punch 

Cutting edge of the punch shall be sharp enough 
to cut holes in the conveyor belts conforming 
IS 1891 ( in various parts ). 

7 SAMPLING 

7.1 Unless otherwise agreed to between the 
supplier and the purchaser, the procedure given 
in IS 2500 ( Part 1 ) : 1973 shall be followed. 

7.2 For dimensions, workmanship and finish, 
the sampling plan with inspection level I and 
acceptable quality level ( AQL ) 2*5 percent as 
given in Table 1 and 2 of IS 2500 ( Part 1 ) : 1973 
shall be followed. 

8 DESIGNATION 

8.1 Belt punch shall be designated by its com- 
monly used name, size of belt fastener for which 
it is used, and number of this Indian Standard. 

Example: 

Belt punch used for fixing a belt fastener 
63 and 76.2 shall be designated as; 

Belt Punch IS 12858-63-76.2 

9 MARKING 

9vl Belt puches shall be marked with manu- 
facturer's name, initials or trade-mark, nominal 
size that is belt fastener for which it is used and 
the number of this Indian Standard. 



IS 12858 : 1989

Standard Mark 

The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian 
Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on 
products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced 
to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, 
testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the pro- 
ducer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to 
that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use 
of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from 
the Bureau of Indian Standards. 



Bureau of Indian Standards 

BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 to 
promote harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality 
certification of goods and attending to connected matters in the country. 

Copyright 

BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in 
any form without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in 
the course of implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or 
grade designations. Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director ( Publications), BIS 

Revision of Indian Standards
